a3c0a387d3.q: What does Jace Bombero say about asking God to make life easier versus asking for guidance as a Christian?
a3c0a387d3.a: Jace explains he no longer asks God to make life easier, using Christ as the ultimate example who endured hardship. He emphasizes that everything is hard—staying in shape or staying out of shape—and it's perspective that matters. He compares growth to muscle development: when you make muscles work hard, they rip and tear and grow stronger. The key is understanding that difficulty is where growth happens.

11eca651f2.q: How does Jace Bombero address the issue of repeating the same prayer requests to God multiple times?
11eca651f2.a: Jace acknowledges he has felt like he was repeating himself in prayer, but he knows God hears and his job is to keep the matter in God's hands in faith. He uses an analogy of a father and son: if a son asks his father to take him to Five Below and the father says yes, repeating the request doesn't change the answer—the father already said he would take care of it. He references the Bible: 'My God shall supply all my needs according to his glory,' emphasizing the need to believe God's promises rather than keep asking.

4c931f0e84.q: Why does Jace Bombero feel he is not reaching as many people as he wants with his music?
4c931f0e84.a: Jace says he has a desire to reach a certain group or amount of people, and sometimes feels like he is not reaching enough. However, he has come to realize that the number of people he reaches is intentional—he only reaches the amount of people that God can trust him to handle. He explains: 'That's the certain amount that I can deal with that God can trust me, and so until I get to a point where he can trust me with more people and more dynamics, it's not going to happen.' He does not want to embarrass God through pride or ego.

a442cffa14.q: What is Jace Bombero's perspective on taking God and blessings for granted in everyday life?
a442cffa14.a: Jace emphasizes that people take God's blessings for granted because society is so spoiled with access to things, relationships, and connections. He illustrates this with an example of a man he knew in Illinois who drove a car that required lifting the hood and moving wires every time he started it, yet remained grateful and never complained, always saying 'God blessed me with this car.' Jace reflects: 'It's very easy to take the things that God does for us and just God in general for granted because we're so spoiled,' noting that looking back 10-20 years shows how much more people have access to now.

4c2bd4741f.q: How should Christians balance complaining to God with praising Him in prayer?
4c2bd4741f.a: Jace explains that you are supposed to come to God as you truly are—complaining, praising, and being thankful. The Bible says God knows what you will say before you even say it, but it is up to you to say it. He compares it to coming to your father: sometimes you come in a bad mood, sometimes in a good mood, but if you have a real relationship, the other person understands where you are coming from. He states: 'If you have a relationship, he knows that you. Just come. All those who are weary, the Bible says, come to me.'
